title: cross-team-engineering-leadership-weekly-staff-notes-2026-07-20
content:
Cross-team engineering leadership weekly staff meeting notes
Date: 2026-07-20
Facilitator: Asha Patel
Attendees: Asha Patel, Miguel Rivera, Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Samir Gupta, Lena Torres (SRE), Ben Cho (Platform), Claire Huang (Console), Ravi Singh (Private Deployments)

Agenda:
- Quick wins + highlights
- Current incidents / risk review
- Release readiness: serving-runtime v1.12.0 (canary -> prod)
- Dedicated/Private deployment updates
- Console and rollout tooling updates
- Cross-team blockers & action items
- AOB

Notes / Highlights:
1) Quick wins
- Serving runtime memory regression from last week has been mitigated: hotfix applied to canary (PR #482). Initial canary traffic shows 18% lower OOM rate. Still monitoring. (Owner: Jordan)
- Batching improvements shipped to Dedicated test cluster showing 7-9% cost reduction for 2k-4k token requests. (Owner: Ben)

2) Incidents / Risks
- Incident summary: Intermittent KV cache invalidation on long-lived sessions (SERV-1234). Symptoms: sudden latency spikes for a subset of customers on dedicated pools. Root cause suspected: race condition between eviction path and async cache refresh. Investigating. (Lead: Miguel)
- Risk: upcoming EC2 spot capacity changes in eu-west-1 might impact auto-burst. Ben to confirm fallback capacity plan by EOD Wednesday.
- SRE noted elevated 95th latency on generator routes for 8k+ seq lengths — tracking to model kernel selection path. (Lead: Lena)

3) Release readiness: serving-runtime v1.12.0
- Release targets: canary -> staged -> prod over next two weeks. Key items still open:
  - Final perf regression tests for FP16 quantized paths (blocker: flaky GPU dispatch test). (Owner: Jordan, ETA: 2026-07-22)
  - Canary run extended to 48h due to KV cache incident overlap. Decision: extend and re-evaluate metrics tomorrow morning. (Decision: extend canary)
- Rollback plan reviewed: automated fallback to v1.11.3 and model-variant routing already tested in dry-run. (Owner: Priya)

4) Dedicated / Private deployments
- Private deployment trial with customer X progressing: installation issues around KMS integration on-prem. Ravi and Solutions Eng scheduled on-site call with customer for 2026-07-23. Action: provide step-by-step KMS checklist.
- Capacity planning: finance requested committed GPU count for Q4 pilot by 2026-07-31. Ben to provide draft numbers.

5) Console & Rollouts
- Console improvements for rollout visibility: Claire demoed new per-route rollback UI and canary health scoring. Small UX feedback noted (quicker access to metric deltas). Dev work scheduled next sprint.
- Observability: token-level cost attribution is live internally; public rollout planned after sanitization and docs update. (Owner: Claire)

6) Applied ML / Model Ops
- Model catalog additions: two community LLMs validated for latency profiles; Applied ML team to publish profiles on Friday. (Owner: Priya)
- Eval infra: automated quality regression alerts tied to gold prompt sets will be enabled for canary runs next week. Need final sign-off from Product.

7) Cross-team blockers
- Blocker: flaky GPU dispatch test causing CI noise and delaying green PRs. Action: create dedicated CI slot for perf tests to avoid queuing conflicts. (Owner: Jordan, ETA: 2026-07-24)
- Blocker: backlog of support tickets about model variant mismatches when fallback occurs. Action: Samir to coordinate a doc + runbook to be linked in Console. (Owner: Samir, ETA: 2026-07-27)

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Miguel: Root-cause analysis for KV cache invalidation (SERV-1234) and proposed fix. Update 2026-07-21 morning.
- Jordan: Stabilize FP16 GPU dispatch tests + ensure canary perf gating is non-flaky. ETA 2026-07-22.
- Ben: Confirm fallback capacity plan for eu-west-1 spot changes. ETA 2026-07-22.
- Priya: Finalize canary rollback runbook and confirm automated fallback tests. ETA 2026-07-21.
- Claire: Ship rollout UI tweaks and prepare internal docs for token-level cost rollout. ETA 2026-07-28.
- Ravi & Solutions Eng: On-site KMS troubleshooting workshop with customer X. Scheduled 2026-07-23.
- Samir: Draft support runbook for model-variant fallback and link to console help. ETA 2026-07-27.

Decisions made:
- Extend v1.12.0 canary to 48h given current KV cache investigation.
- Move FP16 gating to soft-gate with additional monitoring rather than blocking full prod release (temporary measure until tests stabilized).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we require an emergency cap on long-lived session duration to reduce KV cache pressure? (Action: Miguel to propose short-term mitigation)
- Should Finance signoff on Q4 committed GPUs include buffer for private pilot growth? (Ben + Finance meeting 2026-07-21)

Next meeting:
- Weekly cadence — next cross-team leadership staff notes meeting: 2026-07-27 (same time). Focus: release post-mortem if canary rolled, capacity numbers for Q4, and customer X installation status.

Notes to self / informal items:
- Remember to add SERV-1234 RCA to Confluence and tag Product for customer communications.
- Follow up with Product about enabling quality regressions for canary traffic (need sign-off).

Raw links / references mentioned in the meeting:
- SERV incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SERV-1234
- Release notes draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/serve-release-notes-2026-07
- Canary perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482

End of notes.
